description: Two-panel photograph figure of cold-rolled Fe-7 wt.% Al alloy products, imaged as macro specimen photographs rather than plots. (a), labelled top-right, shows on a uniform blue background three rolled products arranged diagonally: two long, narrow, dark grey-to-black strips (plates) with slightly rough matt surfaces, one of them with a ragged/uneven end, and, to the upper right, a shorter, wider rectangular sheet with a smoother, brighter golden-grey metallic surface bearing a small white adhesive label whose printed text is illegible at the supplied resolution. No scale bar or ruler appears in (a). (b), labelled top-right, shows four bright, highly reflective, mirror-finish curled ribbons of thin metal (foils) resting on a pale grey background; they vary in size, the largest at upper left, arranged as short coiled/curved strips that hold a set curl, indicating thin, ductile rolled material. A printed scale bar labelled "2 cm" sits at the bottom of (b), giving the foils dimensions of a few centimetres. Panels (a) and (b) together demonstrate that the cold-rolled alloy can be produced progressively from thick plates and sheets down to very thin foils; no numeric values other than the 2 cm scale bar are printed.

subfigures.description: Macro photograph on a blue background of three cold-rolled products: two long, narrow, dark matt strips (plates), one with an uneven end, and a shorter rectangular sheet with a brighter metallic surface carrying an illegible white adhesive label. No scale bar present.
Macro photograph of four bright, mirror-finish metallic foils curled into short coils of different sizes on a pale background, with a printed 2 cm scale bar at the bottom.

observations.observation: Panel (a) is a photograph of two long narrow dark rolled strips (plates) and one shorter, wider rectangular sheet with a brighter metallic surface on a blue background.
In panel (a) one long plate shows an uneven/ragged end and a dull, slightly roughened grey-black surface, whereas the shorter sheet is smoother and more reflective.
A small white adhesive label is stuck on the short sheet in (a); its printed text is not legible at the supplied resolution.
Panel (b) shows four bright, mirror-like metallic foils rolled into short curled strips of different sizes on a pale grey background.
Panel (b) contains a printed scale bar labelled "2 cm", which is the only numeric annotation in the figure.
The caption states that (a) shows plates and sheet and (b) shows foils of cold-rolled Fe-7 wt.% Al alloy produced by the AIMFC process.
The citing text states that Fe-7 wt.% Al alloy produced by VIM and AIMFC could be cold rolled to thin sheets and foils, which is what Fig. 3 illustrates.

The citing text reports that the final thickness of the hot-rolled plate was 12 mm and that 24-mm-thick forged sections were hot rolled by 50% before cold rolling, giving context to the thick products in (a).
Neither panel carries a magnification or thickness annotation; the only dimensional reference is the 2 cm scale bar in (b).
The curled, self-supporting shape of the foils in (b) indicates thin, ductile cold-rolled material rather than brittle sheet.
